Knowledge of solid-state materials synthesis and use of structure construction software such as Materials Studio, Crystalmaker, Mercury, VESTA, etc.

The project is dedicated to the accelerated discovery of catalytic materials for low-temperature PEM water electrolyzers, utilizing high-throughput synthesis and characterization techniques.
cond_0102.responsibilities:
As a Postdoctoral Appointee, you will play a pivotal role in this exciting endeavor. Your responsibilities will encompass:
Catalysts Synthesis: Utilize your expertise in materials synthesis to develop novel catalysts guided by machine learning algorithms
Catalyst Performance Evaluation: Utilize aqueous electrochemical combinatorial techniques to evaluate the performance of synthesized catalysts, identifying promising candidates for further development
Device-Level Performance Assessment: Integrate promising catalysts into low-temperature fuel cells and electrolyzers, utilizing single-cell testing platforms to evaluate their device-level performance
cond_0102.requirements:
Background in physical electrochemistry and oxygen evolution electrocatalysis
Background in proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer electrocatalyst and electrode characterization
Background in aqueous electrochemical techniques
Familiarity with inorganic and nanomaterial synthesis and crystal structure analysis using XRD Rietveld analysis
Familiarity with solid-state materials synthesis and use of structure construction software such as Materials Studio, Crystalmaker, Mercury, VESTA, etc.
Experience with X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), X-ray scattering (SAXS & WAXS), and X-ray nano-CT characterization of materials is beneficial
Experience with impedance spectroscopy is beneficial
Ability to communicate effectively in written and oral form, and willingness to work as part of a collaborative multi-institutional team
This background is typically gained through formal education in chemistry, materials science, mechanical or chemical engineering, or physics at the Ph.D. Degree level, with 0–3 years of experience, or equivalent practical laboratory experience in the areas described above

Catalysts Synthesis: Work with the team to develop novel catalysts guided by machine learning algorithms, contributing your expertise in materials synthesis.

Ph.D. In chemistry, materials science, mechanical or chemical engineering, or physics with 0-3 years of experience, or equivalent practical laboratory experience in the areas described above

Experience in X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), X-ray scattering (SAXS & WAXS), and X-ray nano-CT characterization of materials

cond_0237.intro: The Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Materials Group at [Company name masked] is seeking to hire a Postdoctoral Appointee to participate in a project that operates within a large DOE consortium of nine U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories. The project is dedicated to the accelerated discovery of catalytic materials for low-temperature PEM water electrolyzers, utilizing high-throughput synthesis and characterization techniques.
cond_0237.responsibilities:
As a Postdoctoral Appointee, you will play a pivotal role in this exciting endeavor. Your responsibilities will encompass:
Catalysts Synthesis: Utilize your expertise in materials synthesis to develop novel catalysts guided by machine learning algorithms
Catalyst Performance Evaluation: Utilize aqueous electrochemical combinatorial techniques to evaluate the performance of synthesized catalysts, identifying promising candidates for further development
Device-Level Performance Assessment: Integrate promising catalysts into low-temperature fuel cells and electrolyzers, utilizing single-cell testing platforms to evaluate their device-level performance
cond_0237.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Working knowledge of physical electrochemistry and oxygen evolution electrocatalysis
Familiarity with proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer electrocatalyst and electrode characterization
Experience with aqueous electrochemical techniques
Background in inorganic and nanomaterial synthesis and crystal structure analysis using XRD Rietveld analysis
Ph.D. In chemistry, materials science, mechanical or chemical engineering, physics, or a related field, or equivalent practical laboratory experience
Around 0–3 years of experience in the areas described, or an equivalent combination of education and hands-on lab work
Ability to communicate effectively in written and oral form, and willingness to work as part of a collaborative multi-institutional team
Preferred Requirements
Experience with solid-state materials synthesis and structure construction software such as Materials Studio, Crystalmaker, Mercury, VESTA, or similar tools
Exposure to X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), X-ray scattering (SAXS & WAXS), and X-ray nano-CT characterization of materials
Background in impedance spectroscopy

cond_0300.responsibilities:
As a Postdoctoral Appointee, you will play a pivotal role in this exciting endeavor. Your responsibilities will encompass:
Catalysts Synthesis: Utilize your expertise in materials synthesis to develop novel catalysts guided by machine learning algorithms
Catalyst Performance Evaluation: Utilize aqueous electrochemical combinatorial techniques to evaluate the performance of synthesized catalysts, identifying promising candidates for further development
Device-Level Performance Assessment: Integrate promising catalysts into low-temperature fuel cells and electrolyzers, utilizing single-cell testing platforms to evaluate their device-level performance

Familiarity with solid-state materials synthesis and use of structure construction software such as Materials Studio, Crystalmaker, Mercury, VESTA, etc.

Experience with impedance spectroscopy is beneficial

The project is dedicated to the accelerated discovery of catalytic materials for low-temperature PEM water electrolyzers, utilizing high-throughput synthesis and characterization techniques.
cond_0505.responsibilities:
As a Postdoctoral Appointee, you will play a pivotal role in this exciting endeavor. Your responsibilities will encompass:
Catalysts Synthesis: Utilize your expertise in materials synthesis to develop novel catalysts guided by machine learning algorithms
Catalyst Performance Evaluation: Utilize aqueous electrochemical combinatorial techniques to evaluate the performance of synthesized catalysts, identifying promising candidates for further development
Device-Level Performance Assessment: Integrate promising catalysts into low-temperature fuel cells and electrolyzers, utilizing single-cell testing platforms to evaluate their device-level performance
cond_0505.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Extensive knowledge of physical electrochemistry and oxygen evolution electrocatalysis
Extensive knowledge of proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer electrocatalyst and electrode characterization
Extensive knowledge of aqueous electrochemical techniques
Excellent written and oral communication skills and the ability to work as part of a collaborative multi-institutional team
Ph.D. In chemistry, materials science, mechanical or chemical engineering, or physics with 0-3 years of experience, or equivalent practical laboratory experience in the areas described above
Preferred Requirements
Knowledge of inorganic and nanomaterial synthesis and crystal structure analysis using XRD Rietveld analysis
Knowledge of solid-state materials synthesis and use of structure construction software such as Materials Studio, Crystalmaker, Mercury, VESTA, etc.
Experience in X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), X-ray scattering (SAXS & WAXS), and X-ray nano-CT characterization of materials
Experience in impedance spectroscopy
